summary: Build green hydrogen project development skills with practical tools, feasibility models, and investment-case templates.
lede: Green hydrogen project development training helps energy-project professionals assess feasibility and shape an investment case. Learners examine renewable resource and production assumptions, build a simplified cost model, compare power-sourcing and market pathways, and consider certification, contract risks, and financing. It is designed for people involved in project origination, investment screening, contracting, or policy analysis who need to evaluate hydrogen opportunities using project data and business-case assumptions.
audienceIntro: This course is built for professionals who already work around energy projects and now need to apply those skills to hydrogen-specific feasibility, economics, and market entry decisions. It is especially relevant if you support project origination, investment screening, contracting, or policy analysis in a hydrogen development context. The content is practical, intermediate-level, and geared to professionals who want to work confidently with hydrogen project data, assumptions, and business cases. Green hydrogen project developers who screen opportunities and shape project concepts. Renewable energy analysts who assess power supply and utilization assumptions. Project finance specialists who test bankability and investment logic. Energy transition managers who coordinate technical and commercial workstreams. Hydrogen strategy leads who brief executives on portfolio options. Power procurement managers who structure renewable electricity supply for electrolysis. Sustainability and ESG specialists who review certification and traceability requirements. Policy and regulatory affairs professionals who track deployment incentives and standards. Process and operations engineers who translate technical inputs into project assumptions. Commercial managers who negotiate offtake and risk allocation terms.
prerequisites: You need a laptop, spreadsheet software, and the ability to work with simple project datasets during exercises. Prior knowledge of renewable energy projects, project finance, or energy policy is helpful, but no coding or specialized software installation is required. If you bring a live or hypothetical hydrogen project, you will get more value from the scenario work and templates.
